title: Coles/woolworths online shopping
body:
O.P.
Just wondering if many people do their grocery shopping online and have it delivered? I find grocery shopping extremely boring and time consuming, so i'm looking into the online delivery options.
Does anyone know how much it usually costs to get say $100 worth of groceries delivered in a metro area? I had a look on the woolies site, but it just said "anywhere between $5 and 18" which doesn't help. What are these delivery costs based on? The number of items, weight, distance etc?
How good are they for fresh items like fruit and veges etc? Do they generally pick out good ones, or are you better off going into the shop to pick them out yourself?
Also if you live in a unit are they likely to bring them upstairs to your door? Or will they just drop them at the bottom of the stairs?
I'd be very interested to know what people's experiences are. If its much more than $5 for delivery then it might not be worth it.

---- replies ----
[User #96238141 postsladidaForum Regular] I was using Coles during October when they had a free delivery promotion. I was really pleased. They carried the groceries in on crates, all in one go. I am in a house and they brought them into my kitchen. I highly doubt that they would just dump your lot at the bottom of the stairs because you're in a unit. The service was really good.
I never brought fruit and veg from them because I'm pretty fussy with quality and tend to go to the markets (though, if someone knows of a good delivery service for them in brisbane, let me know!). I bought meat once and ended up with one massive pork chop rather than two smaller ones like I wanted. It obviously just goes on weight so you just get whatever you pay for. I think I'd prefer to pick something like that out myself in the future (mince and chicken tenderloins were fine though).
When i was looking to order outside of the promotional period, the cheapest delivery coles was offering was $5 on Monday mornings between 9am and midday (i think). The most expensive was $13. They work out the cost based upon the timeslot rather than the amount of groceries you buy. If you go to the Coles wesbite, there a bit where you can type in your postcode and it will bring up a chart of delivery costs.
[User #193179444 postsAnti-FeministIn the penalty box] O.P.

Are the prices for all items exactly the same as you'd pay in the store? Do they have fewer products available online?
[User #2105903586 postsDadAgain...That's not an argument!Whirlpool Forums Addict] I'm a fan of online grocery shopping in the UK.
its CHEAPER than instore because they dont need to dedicate presentation shleving and can run out of a warehouse.
I havent yet used online shopping in Australia for 2 reasons:
1) Its only just available in 'small-town Brisbane what with us only having a population of 2 million (despite being well established overseas a DECADE ago in towns FAR FAR smaller) 2) It costs more! I cant get my head around this – the supermarkets save money by a cheaper distribution model and they STILL ask the customer to bend over, take it painfully and pay MORE?.
[User #96238141 postsladidaForum Regular] The prices are generally the same and they have the same catalogue specials available online as they do in the store. Occasionally they have extra "online only" specials as well.
They don't have all products available online but they do have a really good selection. I would think they would have about 90% of their products available online.
If you want to check it out, you could go through the sign up process with coles and "browse the isles" as it's called. You won't be obligated to purchase anything until you put things in your "trolley" and go through the checkout process. After you put an order in, you also have the option of changing it/cancelling it until about 11pm the night before delivery.

The prices are generally the same and they have the same catalogue specials available online as they do in the store.
Not finding this for Woolworths.
Occasionally they have extra "online only" specials as well.
That I am finding.
They don't have all products available online
I can't believe the amount of common products not available online.
After you put an order in, you also have the option of changing it/cancelling it until about 11pm the night before delivery.
With Woolworths that was not as simple as I thought it would be.
Had to call them, get them to cancel, and then I started again.
All had to be done before the close of the delivery window.
They don't say when it closes on the Website from what I can tell.
Also with Woolworths I am finding the list management is stuffed!
And I can't be stuffed using it again until they fix it and/or make it easier to work with.

[User #122113619 postsDazaWhirlpool Forums Addict] I use Coles online regularly since I have a motorbike. I don't have a problem with them – the delivery window is wide, so I always hope I get the start of the run.
I live in a unit and they walk up the stairs and bring everything inside, which is good. With previous history and been able to add that to your cart, then chop and change, it doesn't take very long at all.
I haven't tried Woolworths yet because I found their delivery charges to be higher.
[User #400430963 poststwoflopsybunniesWhirlpool Enthusiast] it's too expensive. Each grocery item is slightly more expensive online than instore. I looked at just a few and they were 20c-50c more. That adds up.
I have a very strict budget and altho online appeals greatly to me I can't bring myself to wear the extra cost. Also I try to do the majority of my shopping at Aldi.
[User #4090747435 postsLilacLizardooO^O^Oo-<Whirlpool Forums Addict] I drink filtered water that i buy online/get home delivered from an organic food home delivery place & while doing that i also often buy various grocery items at the same time.
Including delivery costs it works out significantly cheaper than buying from coles or woolworths stores, plus it's much more convenient & I've been very happy with produce quality (and I'm someone that picks each individual item with great care)
& yes they bring all 100litres of water right to my unit's door (so do woolworths) if I'm out & inside if I'm home
My advice would be to see if there's smaller companies in your area that have the majority of the product you want. coles/woolies have stores, so no benefit to them in home delivering, smaller companies can save on storefront costs by delivering & so want it to work
